findings.title: Task 14 makes a tokenizer `MemoryError` a per-file skip, which contradicts D3 and Task 11
findings.description: Task 14 lists `MemoryError` among the TypeScript token errors. Under Task 10 those errors send the file to `unparsed_files`. But D3, the failure-mode table and Task 10 all say a `MemoryError` during the pass makes `duplicated_lines` `tool_failed`. Task 11 tests that too ("a tokenizer that raises `MemoryError` gives `tool_failed`"). Which path runs depends on the order of the `except` clauses, so whoever implements it has to guess. The two languages also disagree: Task 12's Python token errors leave `MemoryError` out. 400 does pass `(TypeScriptParseError, MemoryError)` as parse errors (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/typescript_length.py:151`), which is probably where this was copied from. Fix: take `MemoryError` out of Task 14's token errors and say that `measure_duplication` handles `MemoryError` itself, ahead of `token_errors`.

findings.title: Task 13's "function length is unaffected" can't hold for the inputs it names
findings.description: An unterminated triple-quoted string and bad indentation are both `SyntaxError`s for `ast.parse`. Those files are already in function length's `unparsed_files` through `_PARSE_ERRORS` (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/python_adapter.py:81`). A junior agent reading "function length is unaffected" will likely assert that the file's functions are present, and that test can never pass. Restate it: function length's result for the repo is identical to 400's (the file is unparsed there for its own `ast` error), and the duplication pass changes nothing about it.

findings.title: Task 5 doesn't say the complexity walk must be iterative, and the TypeScript parse errors don't include `RecursionError`
findings.description: The failure-mode table says a `RecursionError` in a complexity walk is "already one of the adapter's parse errors". That's true for Python (`_PARSE_ERRORS`). For TypeScript the parse errors are only `(TypeScriptParseError, MemoryError)`. 400's `_extract_functions` uses an explicit `pending` stack (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/typescript_length.py:125-138`), so it never recurses. If Task 5's walk is written recursively, as a "doesn't descend into nested functions" walk naturally is, deeply nested TypeScript will raise an unhandled `RecursionError` and crash the adapter. Fix: Task 5 should require an explicit-stack walk, like `_extract_functions`. Task 9's `RecursionError` case currently names Python only and should do the same.

findings.title: Task 9's `RecursionError` test doesn't assert the WARNING
findings.description: The Technical Requirements say "Failure-mode tests assert both the signal and the outcome for each row of the failure-mode table." Task 9 checks the outcome (the file is in `unparsed_files`) for both the parse-error and `RecursionError` cases, but not the WARNING per file. Every other row's test names its signal. Add the WARNING assertion here.

findings.title: `tool_support.tool_failed` requires a `command` argument that Tasks 10 and 23 don't define
findings.description: `tool_failed(..., *, command: str, ...)` is keyword-only and required. The duplication pass and the coverage reader run no external command, so the implementer will make up a value. A sentence in each task saying what to pass (for example the report path for coverage, or a fixed description for duplication) avoids two different made-up values. Also, `tool_failed` logs a WARNING per call. So a coverage failure logs once in `read_coverage` (Task 21) and once for each of the two metrics. That's harmless, but Task 24's "with a WARNING" assertion should allow more than one.

findings.title: Sequencing, test-with pattern and commit markers are sound
findings.description:
- Each implementation task (3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 19, 21, 23, 25) is followed straight away by its test task, and the commit sits after the test.
- Task 7's refactor commit is backed by 400's existing length tests.
- Dependencies run forward: Task 7's read helper comes before Task 10, Task 18's fixtures before Task 19, and Task 16's parser before Task 21.
- Task 2's explicit metric set stops `take_snapshot` from raising on the new enum members. The test helpers iterate `SnapshotMetric` generically, so "suite passes unchanged" holds.

findings.title: The task list is proportionate, and no load test is needed
findings.description: 30 tasks fits a slice with four metrics across two languages plus a config key and a reader. No task is oversized: the duplication pass, at Effort 4, is a single cohesive module. The slice restates no NFR, so a load test or CI-gating task isn't required. The walkthrough's edits to `.squadron.toml` and the `coverage.xml` it writes are safe, because both files are gitignored (`.gitignore:56`, `.gitignore:174`).
